name: Fruit, vegetable and berry juice powder concentrates (capsules)
short: Title-only 2010 case letter on toxicity, no details. 6-month trial (18 of 34 older adults took it): well tolerated, no safety-relevant change in liver, kidney or metabolic markers.
text: Few data. A 2010 case report published as a letter, available as a title only, pairs a brand name (not repeated here) with the word toxicity; a 2011 trial abstract uses the same brand for an encapsulated juice powder concentrate of fruits and vegetables, but the link cannot be shown in a quote because the brand is not repeated here. The title gives no details of the harm, the dose or the person affected, and it cannot show cause. In an open-label randomized trial in 34 generally healthy older adults (18 in the supplement group, 16 controls), a commercial fruit, vegetable and berry juice powder concentrate supplement taken for 6 months (the pre-specified 6-month point of a 1-year trial) was well tolerated, and markers of liver, kidney, thyroid, lipid and glucose metabolism showed no safety-relevant deterioration; the authors call these findings hypothesis-generating. In a randomized open-label trial in healthy people, an encapsulated fruit, vegetable and berry juice powder concentrate taken together with a plant-based omega-3 supplement raised blood levels of some vitamins and carotenoids without effects on liver, kidney or thyroid function or blood lipids. In an observational study of 28 healthy peri- and postmenopausal women with menopausal symptoms given a nutritional juice supplement (identified in the abstract only by the same brand, not repeated here), no adverse effects were observed. A 2011 systematic review of 22 reports on commercially available mixed fruit and vegetable concentrate supplements found that none reported serious adverse effects; the abstract does not name the products. The abstract of the page's own periodontitis trial reports no safety data. The abstracts do not list the fruits and vegetables or show that these are the same products as the page's capsules. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
